title: Treasury Memo: Rate Uplift on Cash Pickup Shortfall Credits
content:
Where a Cash Pickup payout location paid out at a rate below the rate Paloma disclosed, Paloma's shortfall credit carries an uplift on the shortfall's US-dollar value. The uplift depends on the remedy the customer has chosen on the incorrect-amount notice.

## Uplift schedule

| Customer's choice on the notice | Rate recorded on the payout | Uplift |
|---|---|---|
| a re-issue of the shortfall | below the disclosed exchange rate | 8 percent |
| a refund of the shortfall | below the disclosed exchange rate | 4 percent |
| a re-issue or a refund of the shortfall | equal to or above the disclosed exchange rate | none |
| no choice recorded | any | none |

Where no uplift applies, the shortfall value is left as it is.

## How the uplift acts

The uplift is a percentage of the shortfall's US-dollar value. That value is itself already rounded to the cent. The uplift is applied once to that rounded value, and the product is rounded half up to the cent. The uplifted shortfall value is the rounded US-dollar value multiplied by one plus the uplift percentage divided by one hundred.

The two inputs are read from the transfer's records: the choice recorded on the customer's notice, and the rate applied as recorded on the cash payout. Both are compared with the disclosed exchange rate on the transfer.

## Worked figures (hypothetical shortfall value of 21.62 USD)

- Re-issue chosen, payout rate below the disclosed rate: 21.62 multiplied by 1.08 is 23.3496, rounded half up to 23.35.
- Refund chosen, payout rate below the disclosed rate: 21.62 multiplied by 1.04 is 22.4848, rounded half up to 22.48.
- Re-issue chosen, payout rate equal to the disclosed rate: no uplift, 21.62.
